title: SPARC Bilateral Phrenic Neurophysiology Preparation with Afferent Stimulation
author: Kristi Streeter
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bgfzjtp6
materials: Isolate bilateral phrenic nerves using a dorsal approach:

steps.title: Induce Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia using isoflurane in a closed chamber.

substeps.instruction: Administer 2.5-3% isoflurane in 100% O2 for 3-5 minutes.
Transfer animal to nose cone and maintain at 3% isoflurane in 100% O2.

steps.title: Establish Intravenous Access and Maintenance
steps.instruction: Place a tail vein line and transition to urethane anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Place intravenous line into tail vein for delivery of drugs/anesthesia/fluids; flush with heparinized saline.
Reduce isoflurane to 1%.
Begin urethane infusion (1.8g/kg in ddH2O at 6ml/hr) while slowly decreasing isoflurane.
Confirm adequate plane of anesthesia via toe pinch and transfer to surgical station.

steps.title: Maintain Physiological Stability
steps.instruction: Regulate body temperature and respiratory function.

substeps.instruction: Measure body temperature via rectal probe and maintain at 37.0 +/- 0.5 C via heated surgical table.

Perform tracheostomy and initiate mechanical ventilation with the following parameters: rate = 70 breaths/minute; tidal volume = (0.7 x body weight (in grams)) mL; inspired gases: 50% O2 + a small percentage of CO2 (target end-tidal CO2 ~ 45mmHg) + balance N2.

steps.title: Perform Initial Surgical Procedures
steps.instruction: Perform vagotomy and establish arterial monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Perform bilateral vagotomy.
Place femoral arterial line to monitor arterial blood pressure and withdraw blood samples (pre-fill catheter with heparinized saline, ensuring no bubbles).

steps.title: Insert Femoral Arterial Catheter
steps.instruction: Surgically isolate the femoral artery and insert the catheter.

substeps.instruction: Make a 1/2 inch ventral incision just distal to the groin on the inner thigh to expose the femoral artery, vein, and nerve.
Gently dissect surrounding fascia to isolate the femoral artery.
Tie off the distal end of the femoral artery and place a loose suture at the proximal end.
Use an alligator clamp to pull the suture and temporarily prevent blood flow at the proximal end.
Make a small partial incision into the femoral artery wall and insert the arterial catheter into the proximal portion (~1 cm into the vessel), loosening the proximal suture to enable advancement.
Tie the catheter into the vessel using the proximal suture and secure with additional sutures as needed.
Ensure no kinks in the vessel and open the stopcock to ensure unresisted flow.
Flush the catheter with heparinized saline and connect to the pressure transducer/amplifier.

steps.title: Isolate Phrenic Nerves
steps.instruction: Expose and isolate the bilateral phrenic nerves.

substeps.instruction: Using a cautery, perform a ~2 inch incision just lateral to midline and medial to shoulder blade.
Using a cautery, dissect the dorsal musculature connecting the medial border of the scapulae to the posterior trunk on both sides.
Reflect the medial border of the scapulae and secure with an alligator clip.
Dissect deep thoracic wall muscles and overlying fascia to expose the brachial plexus.
Pass 4.0 suture under the horizontal tendon above the brachial plexus twice and place a basket stitch around the tendon; pull toward midline and secure to open phrenic pocket.
Cut the brachial plexus distally and reflect the nerve bundle to expose the phrenic nerve.
Using fine forceps, isolate the phrenic nerve from surrounding fascia without touching or pulling the nerve.
Section the nerve distally and carefully desheath the proximal end (~1 mm).
Add 0.9% saline to the phrenic pocket.
Repeat the process to isolate the right phrenic nerve.

steps.title: Perform Dorsal Rhizotomy (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform dorsal rhizotomy for designated groups.

substeps.instruction: Cut left C3, C4, C5, and C6 dorsal rootlets.
Using cautery, make a ~1 inch medial incision from the base of the skull.
Cut through underlying muscles to expose vertebral processes.
Use cautery to separate musculature from C2 vertebrae and a microcurette to remove muscles from C3-C6 vertebrae.
Using ronguers, remove the left portion of C3-C6 vertebrae.
Using microscissors and fine forceps, cut and remove dura over C3-C6.
Visualize and cut all dorsal rootlets from C3-C6 with microscissors.
Add saline-soaked cotton above the spinal cord.

steps.title: Set Up Phrenic Nerve Recordings
steps.instruction: Position electrodes and secure the nerve stumps.

substeps.instruction: Place a magnetic base with L-shaped rod running lengthwise with the rat and above the midline.
Pull and wrap suture around both tendons around the rod.
Fill the phrenic cavity with 0.9% saline and suck the distal end of the proximal nerve stump into the suction electrode (the retracted nerve sheath should form a tight seal).
Verify that the nerve tip is visible within the electrode and both the inner wire and desheathed nerve portion are fully submerged in saline.
Place the uninsulated tip of the outer wire against the proximal stump of the nerve (proximal to the electrode tip) and check signal quality.

steps.title: Post-Surgical Stabilization
steps.instruction: Administer fluids and paralytics, then stabilize baseline.

substeps.instruction: Administer fluids at a 4:1 ratio of Lactated Ringers Solution + Sodium Bicarbonate at 1.0 ml/hr.
Administer pancuronium bromide (paralytic): 1g in 1cc delivered via tail vein over 3 minutes.
Set baseline CO2 parameters no sooner than 20 minutes after pancuronium bromide delivery.
Draw an initial blood sample to ensure base excess (SBE) of +/- 3.
Hyperinflate the lungs over 2 respiratory cycles by briefly occluding the expiratory line.
Wait at least 20 minutes before starting the experimental protocol; ensure stable baseline activity for at least 15 minutes (no trend increases/decreases > 5%).
Take a blood sample during baseline (separated by at least 5 minutes) to establish baseline blood gas values: Criteria = PaO2 > 150 mmHg; SBE within +/- 3.
Wait at least 5 minutes after the blood sample before starting the experimental protocol.

steps.title: Experimental Stimulation Protocol
steps.instruction: Deliver biphasic stimulation and record responses.

substeps.instruction: Set inspiratory-triggered stimulation threshold: using contralateral integrated phrenic amplitude, set horizontal cursor in the middle of the phrenic amplitude.
Attach left phrenic electrode to stimulator; record from the right phrenic electrode.
Deliver biphasic, inspiratory-triggered stimulation using either a wide pulse (1.0ms per phase) or narrow pulse (0.1ms per phase).
Deliver stimulation for 20 seconds at a pre-determined current, then turn off and record output for 5 minutes.
Repeat until all 12 currents have been delivered (currents are randomly presented to each animal).
Draw a blood sample after every 4 currents; adjust inspired gas concentrations to keep PaCO2 within 2 mmHg of baseline and PaO2 > 150 mmHg.

steps.title: Final Response and Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform final hypercapnic challenge and analyze data.

substeps.instruction: At the end of the experiment, deliver hypercapnia (12% inspired CO2) for maximum response.

Analyze bilateral phrenic activity (amplitude and frequency), blood pressure (systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressures), and heart rate at baseline, during/after each current, and during hypercapnia.
